headline: ALEPH's own simulation predicts no rise of the mu mu / e mu ratio (b_MC about -0.005 +- 0.012 per GeV) and ALEPH's di-electrons do not rise against the e mu template (b_ee -0.008 +- 0.014), while the muon data rise (0.027 +- 0.012). Neither difference reaches 2 sigma (pulls 1.84 and 1.89), so the simulation and the electrons can neither confirm nor rule out the data's rise; with the simulation's slope the excess is 2.7-2.9 sigma in the conservative bin-by-bin frame.
meaning_applied: Amendment 0.26 sec. 6, 'M1z FAIL': ALEPH's simulation does not predict the rise; the 2.66 -> 1.62 slope result is a feature of the muon data, not a simulation-backed background correction. Its last clause ('2.66 stays our best number') is superseded by NOTE-aprime 0.4 sec. 9 (3.1-3.4 sigma with the smooth background) and is not adopted. 'E1 FAIL with E2 PASS': the di-electrons cannot tell.
